root_cause.text: The ctnetlink netfilter attribute policies failed to enforce valid ranges and bitmasks for TCP protoinfo and conntrack/expect filter fields, allowing out-of-range userspace values—especially TCP window scale values up to 255—to reach kernel logic and be used in undefined operations such as a u32 shift count.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that “the ctnetlink path accepted 0-255, causing undefined behavior when used as a u32 shift count,” and the patch fixes this by replacing plain `NLA_U8`/`NLA_U32` policies with `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., TCP_MAX_WSCALE)` and `NLA_POLICY_MASK(...)`, while removing the prior ad hoc checks like `>= TCP_CONNTRACK_MAX` and `flags & ~MASK`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a kernel-only mask macro for all valid conntrack expectation flags to simplify internal flag handling.
intent_record.what: A new macro definition, NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK, was added under an #ifdef __KERNEL__ guard, combining NF_CT_EXPECT_PERMANENT, NF_CT_EXPECT_INACTIVE, and NF_CT_EXPECT_USERSPACE with bitwise OR in the UAPI header.
intent_record.how: This provides kernel-only code with a single mask constant representing all valid expectation flag bits, enabling simpler validation or masking of expectation flags at runtime while keeping the symbol unavailable to userspace builds.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict conntrack filter flag netlink attributes to valid bits by enforcing a mask-based policy check.
intent_record.what: The netlink attribute policy entries for CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS and CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS were changed from plain `{ .type = NLA_U32 }` definitions to `NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_U32, CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, these two filter flag attributes are now validated against the CTA_FILTER_F_ALL bitmask so only supported flag bits are accepted, rejecting netlink messages that contain unknown or invalid bits instead of allowing any 32-bit value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop rejecting conntrack netlink filter orig/reply flag values by removing unsupported-bit validation in the filter parser.
intent_record.what: The change removes the validation checks that returned -EOPNOTSUPP when filter->orig_flags or filter->reply_flags contained bits outside CTA_FILTER_F_ALL, while keeping the existing assignments from CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS and CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS when those attributes are present.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the parser now accepts any 32-bit values for orig_flags and reply_flags instead of rejecting unsupported flag bits, allowing netlink filter messages with previously disallowed flag combinations to pass through successfully.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS netlink input to valid big-endian masked expectation flags so invalid or unsupported bits are rejected during attribute validation.
intent_record.what: The netlink attribute policy entry for CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS was changed from a plain 32-bit unsigned type declaration `{ .type = NLA_U32 }` to `NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_BE32, NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK)`, introducing a big-endian 32-bit masked policy tied to `NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, validation of the CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS netlink attribute becomes stricter: the attribute is now interpreted as a big-endian 32-bit value and only bits allowed by `NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK` are accepted, rejecting unsupported or invalid flag combinations that previously could pass generic u32 validation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add upper-bound validation for conntrack TCP netlink state and window-scale attributes so invalid values are rejected during parsing.
intent_record.what: The netlink attribute policy entries for CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE, CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_ORIGINAL, and CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_REPLY were changed from plain NLA_U8 type declarations to NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, ...) declarations, adding maximum allowed values of TCP_CONNTRACK_SYN_SENT2 for the TCP state and TCP_MAX_WSCALE for both window scale fields.
intent_record.how: This makes netlink attribute parsing reject TCP state and window scale values that exceed valid protocol-defined ranges, preventing invalid userspace-provided U8 values from being accepted and propagated into conntrack TCP protocol handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the early TCP state range rejection in nlattr_to_tcp() so provided protoinfo state values are accepted instead of failing with -EINVAL.
intent_record.what: The change removes a pre-lock validation block that checked whether CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE was present and whether its nla_get_u8() value was greater than or equal to TCP_CONNTRACK_MAX, and returned -EINVAL if so.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer rejects netlink input containing an out-of-range TCP conntrack state at this point and will proceed to take ct->lock and assign the provided state value when the attribute is present.

grouping_result.intent: Add a kernel-only mask macro for all valid conntrack expectation flags to simplify internal flag handling.
Add upper-bound validation for conntrack TCP netlink state and window-scale attributes so invalid values are rejected during parsing.
Remove the early TCP state range rejection in nlattr_to_tcp() so provided protoinfo state values are accepted instead of failing with -EINVAL.
Restrict CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS netlink input to valid big-endian masked expectation flags so invalid or unsupported bits are rejected during attribute validation.

consistency_review.core_intent: Hunk 4 adds upper-bound validation for conntrack TCP netlink state and window-scale attributes during parsing.
consistency_review.reason: Hunk 1 validates conntrack filter flag attributes using a bitmask policy, which targets a different attribute family and validation rule than the TCP state/window-scale bound checks in the core subset.

consistency_review.core_intent: Relax overly strict netlink conntrack attribute validation by removing premature rejection checks so valid filter/protoinfo values are accepted instead of returning -EINVAL.
Restrict conntrack-related netlink flag attributes to valid bitmasks so invalid or unsupported bits are rejected during attribute validation.
Remove overly strict netlink conntrack attribute validation checks so legitimate user-provided filter/protoinfo values are accepted instead of being rejected with -EINVAL.
Tighten netlink attribute validation for conntrack-related flag fields by masking allowed bits and rejecting invalid or unsupported flags.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds an internal kernel mask macro for expectation flags to simplify internal handling. It does not enforce userspace attribute validation, valid ranges, or bitmask checking on ctnetlink protoinfo/filter inputs, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.

The vulnerability is caused by missing range validation for TCP protoinfo netlink attributes, especially TCP window-scale values. This group explicitly adds upper-bound checks for conntrack TCP state and window-scale attributes during parsing, directly addressing that root cause.

The vulnerability stems from missing/insufficient validation of netlink conntrack/protoinfo attributes. This group changes those exact validation paths by removing checks on filter flag bitmasks and TCP protoinfo state ranges, directly affecting whether out-of-range userspace values are rejected or allowed into kernel logic.

The vulnerability is caused by missing netlink attribute range/bitmask validation for conntrack/expect-related fields. This group specifically adds mask-based validation for conntrack filter flags and CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS, directly addressing the root cause of invalid userspace values reaching kernel logic.

candidates.rationale: This policy accepted any 8-bit userspace value for the original TCP window scale without enforcing the valid TCP window scale range, allowing out-of-range values such as 255 to enter kernel logic.

This policy likewise lacked an upper-bound check for the reply-direction TCP window scale, permitting invalid values to pass netlink parsing and later be used in undefined operations such as oversized shifts.
The TCP protoinfo state attribute policy only checked type, not a valid state range, so invalid TCP state values from userspace were not rejected at attribute-validation time.

This filter policy allowed any 32-bit orig-flags value with no mask restriction during netlink attribute validation, matching the root cause of failing to enforce valid bitmasks for conntrack filter fields.

This expectation-flags policy accepted arbitrary 32-bit values instead of restricting input to valid supported flag bits, directly reflecting the missing bitmask enforcement described in the root cause.

This TCP protoinfo state policy only enforced the attribute type and not the valid state range, so out-of-range TCP state values from userspace were not rejected during netlink parsing.
This conntrack filter policy accepted arbitrary 32-bit orig-flags values without enforcing a valid bitmask, matching the root cause of missing bitmask validation for filter fields.

This expectation-flags policy allowed arbitrary 32-bit values instead of restricting userspace input to supported flag bits, directly reflecting the missing mask enforcement described in the root cause.
